chunks: Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said, concerning a man who said to his wife, “I did not find you a virgin”: “He is to be beaten.” I said: “Then if he repeats it?” He said: “He is to be beaten, for he is likely to desist.”

key_terms.اِمْرَأَتِهِ: his wife; the woman against whom the statement was made
key_terms.عَادَ: he repeated the act or returned to saying it again
key_terms.عَذْرَاءَ: a virgin woman; here, the basis of the husband’s defamatory claim
key_terms.يَنْتَهِيَ: to desist or stop; indicating the deterrent purpose of the punishment
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: he is to be beaten; a disciplinary punishment imposed for the offense

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man tells his wife, "I did not find you a virgin"?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who accuses his wife by saying that he did not find her a virgin. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that he is to be punished by beating, and if he repeats the offense, the punishment is repeated as a deterrent.
